subject: BlueHorizon private deployment: sudden p95 latency and 3xx/5xx errors — need exec sync
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluehorizonhealth.com>
To: ops@bluehorizonhealth.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: ceo@bluehorizonhealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 22:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Anomalous latency & 3xx spikes on private cluster

Hi team,

We just observed a major regression on our private VPC deployment around 21:45 UTC. P95 has jumped from ~150ms to ~1.2s and we're seeing a wave of 3xx and intermittent 5xx responses from the inference nodes. This is affecting multiple production routes (chat and streaming gen).

I attached a small sample of logs and stack traces (service-logs-20271119.tar.gz). Can someone confirm if there were any rollout changes or infra events on Redwood's end? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is impacting our call center and an upcoming batch of NPS surveys.

-Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
CTO, BlueHorizon Health
From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluehorizonhealth.com>, ops@bluehorizonhealth.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 22:33:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Anomalous latency & 3xx spikes on private cluster

Thanks for the alert, Sanjay — we see the traces you attached. I'm escalating to our on-call infra and the performance team now.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- We will validate whether any model/pinning/quantization changes occurred in your tenant in the last hour.
- Collect node-level telemetry and inspect RPC/worker queue depths.
- If capacity pressure is confirmed, we can apply a short-term scale-up (hot nodes) or route to a fallback quantized variant to reduce latency.

I've looped in Vivek and Rishi for kernel/runtime investigation and Marissa for customer comms. We'll get back within 30 mins with an initial diagnosis.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 22:50:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Anomalous latency & 3xx spikes on private cluster

Quick triage notes (initial):
- No model rollouts or config changes in BH tenant between 21:00-21:50 UTC based on control plane events.
- Observed a burst of long-lived KV cache misses coincident with p95 jump; cold KV eviction rate increased on 3 host slots.
- RPC queuing increased on worker-02 and worker-04; these two nodes show elevated GPU kernel retries (possible memory fragmentation after a heavy decode workload).
- 3xx responses appear to be our internal throttling codes triggered by request rejection during heavy queueing.

Immediate recommendation: temporarily scale +2 hot nodes (same GPU family) and enable conservative prefix KV warmup for the high-traffic routes. This should drop p95 under 300ms while we continue root-cause.

I will start the scale action now and post the update.

— Vivek
Principal Systems Engineer
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluehorizonhealth.com>, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 00:05:41 -0800
Subject: Re: Anomalous latency & 3xx spikes on private cluster

Hi Sanjay — quick heads up: Vivek has initiated a +2 node scale on your Dedicated pool. We're also enabling a conservative KV prefix warmup for the two affected routes and reducing batch windows from 20ms to 8ms for chat to lower tail latency.

We expect measurable improvement within ~8-12 minutes after nodes join. We'll send logs & a short postmortem once we stabilize. Also scheduled a 09:00 PT call tomorrow (timezone note) to walk through the RCAs and permanent mitigations — joining details below.

Dial-in: https://meet.redwood.com/bh-ops-20271120
Call recording & diagnostic upload: https://drive.redwood.com/bluehorizon/diagnostics-20271119

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluehorizonhealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@bluehorizonhealth.com, ceo@bluehorizonhealth.com
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 00:18:09 -0800
Subject: Re: Anomalous latency & 3xx spikes on private cluster

Thank you for the rapid response. We're seeing immediate improvement (p95 down to ~260ms) but still catching intermittent 3xx for streaming gen. Two asks from us:
1) Can Redwood commit to a temporary SLA credit if we see one more production-impacting incident in the next 7 days? We need assurance given this occurred during a customer-facing campaign.
2) Requesting a short executive sync in the 09:00 PT slot tomorrow — Sanjay and our COO will join. Can someone from Redwood leadership join (VP/GM level)?

Appreciate the team. We'll share a few example traces if anything else pops.

— Sanjay
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@bluehorizonhealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Anomalous latency & 3xx spikes on private cluster

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the update and for offering traces. I can join the 09:00 PT exec sync tomorrow; our VP of Customer Success (Rahul Varma) will also be available to join if you’d like company-level representation.

On SLA credit: I'll coordinate with Finance & Sales to draft a one-time service credit proposal contingent on the postmortem findings. We won't commit to a final amount before we finish the RCA, but we will prioritize resolution and remediation items.

Action items before the call:
- Redwood: finish node-level root cause analysis, attach full logs and kernel traces to the shared drive. (Rishi & Vivek)
- BlueHorizon: share 3 example production traces that still show 3xx/streaming drops (Sanjay).
- CS: prepare short timeline and mitigations slide for the exec meeting (Marissa & Lauren).

See you tomorrow.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success
